title: The Shelter Notice
subtitle: The transit hub night shelter is ordered closed in winter; the order is lawful and the cold is real
coldOpen: 17:00. A notice closes the hub night shelter from tonight.
17:30. Ninety people with blankets outside the hub.

briefing.grievance: Ninety people who sleep at the hub shelter are told it closes tonight for “renovation and security”. Shopkeepers wanted it gone; the transit authority signed. Nobody arranged anywhere else.
knownFacts: The closure notice is signed and lawful; it gives no alternative.
The shelter holds 120; tonight’s forecast is four degrees.
Two shopkeeper complaints and one theft report are on file.
unverifiedClaims: A post says shelter residents stabbed a vendor last week.
A message says the shelter is being sold to a hotel chain.
briefing.responsibility: You run the urban services desk. The order is on your desk and so are ninety people.
briefing.objective: Keep ninety people warm tonight, answer the shopkeepers’ real complaints, and fix the order rather than the people.

rightsMoments.question: A lawful notice closes a shelter in a cold wave with no alternative. What does the right to life require of the authority?

options.text: Not to close without an alternative: shelter in a cold wave is part of the right to life, so the order must be amended or suspended.
options.feedback: Correct. A lawful power must still be exercised consistently with the right to life and dignity.

options.text: To enforce the notice; it is lawful, and the weather is not the authority’s problem.
options.feedback: Lawful powers cannot be used to expose people to life-threatening cold with no alternative.

options.text: To move the residents out of the city so the shelter can close.
options.feedback: Citizens cannot be removed from their own city; out of sight is not a lawful remedy.

rightsMoments.principle: The right to life and dignity (Article 21) includes shelter in life-threatening conditions; a lawful closure power must be exercised with a real alternative in place.
rightsMoments.why: A hall unlocked till half past seven and an amended order kept ninety people alive and the renovation on schedule.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)

simple.question: A legal notice closes a shelter in a cold wave with no other place to go. What must the authority do?

options.a: Not close it without a warm alternative. Change or pause the order.
options.b: Enforce it. The weather is not their problem.
options.c: Move the residents out of the city.

feedback.a: Yes! A legal power still has to protect life.
feedback.b: No. A rule cannot put people in deadly cold with nowhere to go.
feedback.c: People cannot be removed from their own city.

simple.principle: Shelter in deadly cold is part of the right to life. A closure needs a real alternative first.
simple.why: An unlocked hall and a fixed order kept ninety people alive and the repairs on schedule.
